title: Keyboard Manager does not remap the Copilot key correctly in some applications
author: akash3911

status.label: Needs elevation comparison
status.detail: Every named failing target is elevated, but the issue does not say whether PowerToys was also running elevated.

next_action.label: Request elevation comparison

judgment.rationale: The remap works in a normal application and fails in targets reported as Administrator PowerShell, Administrator Git Bash, and Task Manager. That pattern may involve integrity boundaries, but the live report does not state PowerToys' elevation or prove that every target is elevated.
evidence: Win+Shift+F23 to Ctrl works in Notepad and fails in Administrator PowerShell, Administrator Git Bash, and Task Manager.
The issue does not state whether PowerToys is running as administrator.
Open Issue 15241 tracks UIAccess/elevation-related behavior, while Issue 35808 and Issue 45453 are related Copilot-key remap reports.
A third-party workaround comment does not establish a PowerToys root cause or fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether PowerToys is elevated and request one matched-elevation retest; request a diagnostic archive only if that comparison still fails.

issue_context.summary: A Copilot-key shortcut remap works in normal applications but leaks original Windows-key behavior in elevated applications.
known_information: The source is Win+Shift+F23 and the target is Ctrl.
The reporter explicitly names Administrator PowerShell and Administrator Git Bash, and also names Task Manager.
The remap works in Notepad on the same machine.
The report does not say whether PowerToys is elevated or state Task Manager's elevation state.
inferences: An integrity-level boundary is a plausible explanation to test, not a confirmed root cause.
The third-party Copilot Key+ comment does not establish a PowerToys fix.
issue_context.analysis: More screenshots or generic key details would not change triage. A matched-elevation comparison is decisive: success supports an environment/integrity explanation, while continued failure creates a focused Copilot-key remapping investigation. The proposed action does not claim which outcome will occur.

actions.label: Request elevation comparison

comment.body: Thanks for showing that Win+Shift+F23 to Ctrl works in Notepad but fails in Administrator PowerShell, Administrator Git Bash, and Task Manager. Please confirm whether PowerToys itself shows “Running as administrator”, then repeat the test after restarting PowerToys as administrator against one named target that you have confirmed is elevated. If it still fails with matched elevation, add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately after the test and name that exact target. This comparison will determine whether to investigate the remap path further; it does not assume the current cause.
